svg.title: Kitchen lighting: 12 V RGB minimum breadboard layout
svg.desc: Minimum short-strip experiment using an Arduino Nano 33 IoT, three AO3400A SOT-23 MOSFETs soldered to upright SIPK03-1 adapters stacked on the right, barrel jack J0, and two Würth 615004144121 female RJ11 output jacks J1/J2. Adapter header holes are exact; adapter faces and RJ11 mounting/pin fan-outs are conceptual illustrations. AO3400A package pins are 1=gate, 2=source, 3=drain; SIPK03-1 header order is gate-drain-source, occupying separate breadboard rows. Both jacks connect in parallel: pin 2 positive, pin 3 red, pin 4 green, pin 5 blue. Nano D3, D5 and D6 run in parallel outside the right power rails, each through a 2.2 kohm series resistor to its MOSFET gate. No gate drivers, bypass capacitors or pulldown resistors are fitted. Gates can float during Nano startup/reset; initialize the PWM outputs LOW before enabling the lights. Series resistors limit initial nominal GPIO gate-charge current to about 1.5 mA; use ordinary low-frequency PWM. Output positive connects to J0 pin 1 by soldered pigtails, bypassing breadboard contacts; row 40 is unused. J0 is shifted one column right, with its positive and ground jumpers connected to the left rails. The left positive rail and right ground rail have midpoint bridges; the lower ground rails are linked at row 39. Both right positive rail halves and the upper-left ground rail are unused. Nano VIN connects to the left + rail at row 15; Nano GND connects to the right - rail at row 12. Strip returns still pass through breadboard contacts and MOSFETs, never through Nano GPIO. The two ports share a combined 25 cm / 0.30 A LED load limit. All wires are drawn.
svg.text: RGB outputs · ≤25 cm combined · ≤0.30 A total

svg.text: Solder AO3400As to SIPK03-1 adapters; fit their included 0.1″ headers.
No pull-downs: gates may float during startup/reset. Set PWM LOW first.
Upright adapter faces and RJ11 mounting are illustrated schematically.
Positive bypass only; RGB returns use the breadboard. 0.30 A combined.
